summary: Environment A direct-binary verification for the Phase 6.8 Windows rebuild (unified-queue Edit support) - the eighth and last Phase 6 (Operator Ergonomics) slice, and the fifth frontend-only rebuild after 6.2/6.3/6.6/6.7.
buildResult: Rust build succeeded (whisper-rs-sys ggml lib-name two-pass fix applied as expected on the first-attempt failure, exactly as every prior rebuild); pnpm build (tsc -b && vite build) succeeded producing a fresh dist/assets bundle; NSIS packaging finished with the three runtime DLLs confirmed present by the script's own built-in check.
extractionMethod: 7z x against the built installer into a scratch directory; confirmed exit code 0 and listed contents.

symbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings/nm against the extracted cip-desktop.exe, re-run for every prior-phase symbol/string this project has established as a regression tripwire. This phase touched zero Rust files (confirmed via git status before the rebuild), so every count below is expected to be byte-for-byte unchanged from the Phase 6.7 baseline - no new symbols expected.

whisper_full_with_state.note: Stable at 93 for a seventh consecutive rebuild (Phase 6.2 through 6.8), further confirming the Phase 6.2 96->93 drift was one-time compiler-generated auxiliary-symbol non-determinism, not anything phase-specific - the one real exported T symbol has been 1 and unchanged throughout.

symbolRegressionCheck.conclusion: Every prior-phase Rust-side symbol/string count is exactly unchanged. Zero Rust regression, consistent with this phase touching no Rust files.

frontendTextSearch.note: Like Phase 6.7, this phase introduced no genuinely new frontend strings - IntelligenceCard's new edit UI reuses the exact same 'Edit'/'Save'/'Cancel' button labels and 'Edit reference' aria-label Diagnostics Mode's SuggestionCard already has (ACTION_LABELS.edit = 'Edit' is a new map entry, but the string value itself is not new to the compiled bundle). Searching for 'Edit reference' and the standard control string ('Needs Attention') both return 0 matches, reproducing the established Tauri-frontend-bundle tooling limitation - it says nothing about correctness either way here, since there is no new text to distinguish a real hit from a control miss.
frontendTextSearch.conclusion: Correctness for this phase's frontend-only change rests on npm run typecheck's success, the fresh Vite build producing a new asset bundle hash, the installer's SHA-256 changing from the Phase 6.7 baseline, and the full 258/258 frontend test pass (257 pre-existing + 1 new) already recorded in pilot-evidence/6.8/build/unified-queue-edit-support-evidence.json.

architecturalSafetyNotes: Zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema changes - confirmed by this phase touching no Rust files. edit_suggestion (Phase 3.5) is reused entirely unchanged.
The unified queue's Edit reuses the exact same editingId/editValue state Diagnostics Mode's Pending Suggestions panel already uses - no new state to verify at the binary level.
resolveUnifiedShortcutAction's A/R keyboard shortcuts are unaffected by edit's position in actionsFor('bible') - verified by a dedicated unit test, not a binary search.
environmentCStatus: NOT YET VERIFIED for this exact artifact - the decisive pending gate is the operator's own real-hardware test: with a Bible reference in the Needs Attention queue, click Edit, confirm the action buttons are replaced by an input pre-filled with the current reference, type a different valid reference, click Save, and confirm the queue updates; confirm A/R still display/reject the top item exactly as before, unaffected by Edit's presence.
